opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access; their role does not own Source Code so admin is not applicable. Requested write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E005 shows contractor with basic security training (note: this conflicts with HR's full-time classification). Contractors with basic training max out at read access; requested write is above policy, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: There is conflicting evidence on employee E005's status. HR's note classifies Casey Wu as full-time (which would permit write), while Security's note classifies the employee as a contractor with only basic security training and explicitly flags the conflict with HR. Under the contractor policy, basic training caps access at read; write is above that maximum. Granting read is compliant under both interpretations (read is at or below the maximum in either case), and is the more conservative, defensible level. Therefore, grant read access to Source Code.
